description: The second annual counter-protest to Denver's Police Appreciation Day devolved into hours of confrontation, a concussion grenade detonated feet from journalists, and police escorting fascists home. A first-person account from the streets.

faqs.answer: No Party for the Pigs was the annual counter-protest to Denver's Law Enforcement Appreciation Day, organized by local activists to confront and disrupt the celebration of policing. The second iteration took place on July 18, 2021 at Civic Center Park.
faqs.question: What was No Party for the Pigs?

faqs.answer: Lee Keltner was a man killed during a confrontation between dueling rallies at Denver's Civic Center Park on October 10, 2020, during a Patriot Muster that was met by a BLM-Antifa Soup Drive counter-protest. His death cast a shadow over the following year's events.
faqs.question: Who was Lee Keltner?

faqs.answer: When pro-police attendees left the fenced event, antifascist groups followed and confronted the more aggressive far-right attendees. One fascist detonated a concussion grenade approximately four feet from where the author was filming. Police responded by clearing antifascist protesters — who were the victims of the explosion — and providing armed escorts to the fascists who had thrown the grenade.
faqs.question: What happened when the event ended?

faqs.answer: Activists distributed tiny squeeze toys shaped like pigs, each labeled with the name of a Denver police officer known for committing violence against protesters. The author received two pigs named Mendez and Nelsen — officers who had both shot him with large rubber projectiles at previous protests he was covering.
faqs.question: What were the toy pigs?

leadParagraph: On July 18, 2021, Denver's Civic Center Park became a militarized zone as police fenced off their own appreciation rally from counter-protesters. Hours of taunting through chain-link ended with a concussion grenade detonated four feet from an embedded journalist, police blaming the victims, and armed escorts for the fascists who threw it. This is what happens when the state celebrates its own violence.

mainImage.alt: Alt right bootlickers toss flash bang grenade approx. 4ft from me while I am filming & clearly labeled as Press.

methodology: First-person gonzo journalism account based on direct eyewitness experience by Edward Tivrusky, who was embedded with counter-protesters at the July 18, 2021 event. The author was shot by Denver police officers Mendez and Nelsen with rubber projectiles at prior protests, and had a concussion grenade detonated approximately four feet from his position while filming. Supporting sources include 9NEWS, The Denver Post, NPR, The Independent, Fox News, and Denverite coverage of related Denver protest events.
